_README: Sensor -> VANA Data Interface Map. Workstream 6 deliverable, assigned by Arya Barge 2026-08-27. Maps each hardware output concern onto the field the FROZEN V2.2 contract already defines. Where the contract has no field for a real hardware concern it is recorded as an open gap for the contract owner - never invented here.
_owner: Hemanth Reddy - VANA Integration & Data Interface, Group 3
_authority_boundary: Group 3 may design implementation mappings but may not silently create canonical schema or provenance rules. TMS strategy / GC governance / MDU schemas, provenance and identity / Group 3 hardware implementation. Every gap below is addressed to its owner, not resolved unilaterally.
_headline: 9 of 10 Workstream 6 concerns are ALREADY carried by the frozen V2.2 contract and need mapping, not new semantics. 4 require a contract-owner ruling before field hardware emits.
_retry_model_status: SOLVED AND PROVEN LIVE. IK-<observation_id> with 201 -> 200 -> 409 was demonstrated end to end against Group 1's deployed instance on 2026-08-25, 13/13 checks. The edge device implements it; no design work remains.

interface_map.hardware_mapping_note: A numeric reading goes in measurement with a real unit; the numeric-requires-unit rule is enforced in both the bare and object forms. An image or point cloud goes in raw_artifact with measurement carrying the descriptive form.
interface_map.blocked_on: Workstream 1 - the actual measurements the first unit must sense.

interface_map.hardware_mapping_note: Three distinct roles already exist. For a field sensor: observation_timestamp is when the sensor took the reading and MUST NOT change if the send is delayed; source_timestamp is the device's own reported instant; ingestion_timestamp is Group 1's and Group 3 emits null. A large observation->ingestion delta is therefore already the expressible signal of a delayed send - no new field needed.

device_id is the physical device for real hardware. The G3-EXT-<PROVIDER>-<NN> convention is for EXTERNAL providers only and must NOT be used for a Group 3 sensor - a G3-EXT- prefix is contractually bound to capture_method external_api. A field unit uses a real device identifier and capture_method sensor or ground.

Nested location with latitude/longitude/altitude_m/gnss_status/position_accuracy_m, WGS84/EPSG:4326. gnss_status and position_accuracy_m are STRUCTURALLY INAPPLICABLE for external_api but become live fields with real values for hardware - an earlier acceptance record already proved FIX / 0.25 m / 45.2 m persist. If there is no fix, latitude and longitude may be null ONLY with quality_state UNCERTAIN.
The composite tuple. A ground sensor is NOT a flight: flight_id EXT is reserved for external sources, so a fixed ground unit needs a ruling on what occupies the third segment. See OPEN GAP W6-3.

A reference to the preserved original evidence. For a sensor this is the stored reading or image on the edge device, then its uploaded location. The bytes MUST be persisted at capture time - Group 3 already learned this the hard way on 2026-08-25 when an Open-Meteo response was hashed but not stored, leaving the hash unverifiable.

sha256 over the actual captured bytes, computed ON THE EDGE DEVICE before transmission so the hash covers what the sensor produced rather than what survived the network. artifact_type is mandatory; checksum may be null ONLY where hashing is genuinely unsupported, and a placeholder checksum is prohibited.

provenance requires device_id, mission_id, captured_at and raw_artifact, each agreeing with the top-level value. provenance_reference is the separate reviewer-facing pointer. Both now persist and are returned by Group 1 - verified 2026-08-26.

ALREADY SOLVED AND PROVEN LIVE. IK-<observation_id> with the 201 ACCEPTED -> 200 IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY -> 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT sequence is the retry model. A field unit that retries after a dropped connection sends the same key and gets 200, not a duplicate. A unit that retries with MUTATED content gets 409 and cannot corrupt the canonical record. This needs no design work - it needs implementing on the edge device.
NOT COVERED BY THE CONTRACT. See OPEN GAP W6-1. The idempotency key makes the eventual replay safe, but the SEMANTICS of a late arrival are undefined.

open_gaps_for_contract_owner.title: Offline / store-and-forward semantics are undefined
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.evidence: A full-text search of the frozen schema finds no occurrence of offline, store-and-forward, buffer, backfill, late arrival or retry.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.why_it_matters: A field unit will lose connectivity. When it reconnects it may flush hours of buffered readings. Each carries its own observation_id so they are distinct records, and the idempotency key makes replay safe - the MECHANICS are fine. What is undefined is whether a consumer should treat a reading whose ingestion_timestamp is six hours after its observation_timestamp differently from a fresh one.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.who_it_actually_affects: Group 2. Their temporal-applicability ruling already turns on time windows - it ruled GAP on the LiDAR observation for being outside 2020-2023. A delayed field reading could be ruled differently purely because of transport delay rather than anything about the measurement.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.group3_position: The delta between observation_timestamp and ingestion_timestamp is ALREADY expressible and needs no new field. What is needed is a RULING on how a consumer should read it. That is a contract-owner and Group 2 question, not a Group 3 one.

open_gaps_for_contract_owner.title: The clock-trust instruction in the contract is STALE and unfollowable
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.evidence: CORRECTED FINDING. Group 3's first pass claimed clock trust was not expressible at all. That was wrong and the audit caught it: observation_timestamp's own description already says 'If the clock cannot be trusted the observation carries data_state UNCERTAIN; a time is never invented', and source_timestamp says it may be null only where the clock could not be trusted. The mechanism EXISTS. The defect is that it is now unfollowable - data_state was narrowed to RAW/CAPTURED/INGESTED by the contract owner's 2026-08-22 ruling, and UNCERTAIN moved to quality_state. The DESCRIPTION was not updated with the enum. A producer that follows the description emits a value the schema rejects.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.why_it_matters: This is precisely the field-hardware case. For an external_api observation the SOURCE reports the time. For a field sensor the DEVICE reports it, and a unit whose RTC reset on power loss is the single most likely bad timestamp VANA will ever see. The contract anticipated it - and then the instruction for handling it was invalidated by an unrelated amendment. The first hardware producer to hit an untrusted clock will follow the description and be rejected.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.concrete_failure: A field unit loses power, its clock resets, and the edge software correctly detects it cannot trust the time. Following observation_timestamp's description it sets data_state UNCERTAIN - and the payload is REJECTED, because data_state now only accepts RAW/CAPTURED/INGESTED. The honest producer is punished and the dishonest one, which emits a plausible wrong timestamp with data_state CAPTURED, sails through.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.group3_position: No new field is needed and none is proposed. The fix is a DESCRIPTION correction the contract owner already effectively made in 2026-08-22: the untrusted-clock marker is quality_state UNCERTAIN, not data_state UNCERTAIN. Correcting the two descriptions makes the existing mechanism followable again with zero schema change and zero wire change. A secondary question the owner may want to consider separately: the mechanism is binary (trusted / not trusted) and cannot distinguish a GNSS-disciplined clock from a free-running-but-plausible one. That is a lesser gap and not blocking.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.owner: Arya Barge (contract owner) - description correction, not a semantic change

open_gaps_for_contract_owner.title: A fixed ground sensor has no defined third identity segment
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.evidence: observation_id pattern is ^[A-Z0-9]+-Z[0-9]{1,2}-(F[0-9]{1,3}|EXT)-[A-Z0-9]+-OBS[0-9]{3,}$. The third segment accepts F### (a flight) or EXT (an external non-flight source). A fixed ground sensor is neither.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.why_it_matters: Using F### would assert a flight that did not happen - exactly the fabrication the EXT amendment was created to prevent on 2026-08-22. Using EXT would assert an external third-party source, which a Group 3 sensor is not.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.group3_position: This is the same shape of problem the EXT amendment solved, and it should be solved the same way: an additive marker under contract-owner ruling. Group 3 does not create it unilaterally.

open_gaps_for_contract_owner.title: hardware_verified is not returned by Group 1 - blocks the PHYSICAL gate
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.evidence: Live GET 2026-08-27: hardware_verified is absent from the canonical response. Persistence matrix classification: UNDETERMINED.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.why_it_matters: The frozen contract makes synthetic_state PHYSICAL conditional on hardware_verified true. synthetic_state IS persisted. So a sensor can emit PHYSICAL, Group 1 will store PHYSICAL, and a downstream consumer will see a physical-evidence claim with no way to verify the flag that justified it.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.why_it_has_not_bitten: No Group 3 observation has ever been PHYSICAL. Every one to date is CONTROLLED or SYNTHETIC, so the gate has never been exercised. It goes live on the first real sensor reading.
open_gaps_for_contract_owner.group3_position: Group 1 stores and returns hardware_verified before the first PHYSICAL emission.

compatibility_evidence._note: Every classification derived from Group 1's LIVE canonical GET, not from a document. This is the Runtime Integration/Compatibility Evidence half of the deliverable for the Group 1 boundary.

what_is_NOT_proven: No Group 3 sensor has produced a recorded reading. 0 of 8 quadruped actuators are mounted. Oak-D Pro and T-Motor 4-in-1 are classified PRESENT, not VERIFIED, per Suraj's hardware boundary ruling. This map describes the boundary a field unit MUST meet; it does not claim any field unit exists.
